report:
### Conclusion
Yes, regular intake of cranberry juice or cranberry extract can help reduce the risk of recurrent cystitis (urinary tract infections) in women.

### Key Evidence & Mechanisms
* **Mechanism of Action:** Cranberries contain proanthocyanidins (PACs), natural compounds that inhibit *Escherichia coli* (*E. coli*) bacteria from adhering to the epithelial lining of the bladder.
* **Clinical Efficacy:** A comprehensive 2023 Cochrane Systematic Review evaluating 50 randomized controlled trials (with over 8,800 participants) found that cranberry products reduce the risk of symptomatic, culture-verified recurrent UTIs in women by approximately 26% compared to placebo or no treatment.
* **Juice vs. Extract:** Both cranberry juice and standardized cranberry extracts (tablets or capsules) demonstrate preventive benefits. However, adherence is often better with extracts because commercial juice blends can be high in sugar and acidity, occasionally causing gastrointestinal discomfort.
* **Prophylactic Role Only:** Cranberry products are preventive agents and cannot cure an active bacterial infection. Active cystitis requires medical diagnosis and appropriate antibiotic treatment.

### Sources
* Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (PMC): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10108827/
* Cochrane Summary: https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001321_cranberries-preventing-urinary-tract-infections
* Mayo Clinic: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/urinary-tract-infection/symptoms-causes/syc-20353447
